document_title: SPACER, an AI model from MD Anderson, on what may keep T cells out of tumors
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Why do some tumors keep T cells out?

MD Anderson and other Texas institutions built an AI model called SPACER that helps explain where immune cells go and why they avoid some places. It reads gene activity across neighboring cells in intact tissue.

One answer may be mucins, sugar coated proteins many cancers make. They may help wall T cells off. In several melanoma and gastric cancer datasets more mucin was associated with poorer responses to checkpoint inhibitors. The release reports no diagnostic use.

SPACER ran on 37 datasets. In the team's benchmarking it was four to 21 times more effective than existing approaches at finding signals linked to cell recruitment. The Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas helped fund the study.

Could a mucin reading tell a doctor whether a checkpoint drug will work?

#MDAnderson #CPRIT #SpatialTranscriptomics

S2.headline: It reads gene activity where it happens
S2.body: SPACER uses spatial transcriptomics, which measures gene activity inside intact tissue and shows which genes are active and where. Each glass slide drawn here stands for one dataset. Drawn to illustrate.

S6.headline: Immune cells seem to answer signals close by
S6.body: SPACER reads groups of neighboring cells. Tumors expressing antigen presentation genes were more likely to attract T cells. Those genes help cells show protein fragments to immune cells. Drawn to illustrate.

S7.headline: A sugar coat that may be a wall
S7.body: Mucins are large sugar coated proteins many cancers make. The researchers found evidence mucins may help form physical barriers that keep T cells away from tumors. Drawn to illustrate.

S8.headline: More mucin went with poorer response
S8.body: In several melanoma and gastric cancer datasets, more mucin went with poorer responses to checkpoint inhibitors, drugs that help T cells kill cancer cells better. An association in existing data. Drawn to illustrate.
